Pooled parameter estimates

Source: R/pooled.R
pooled_estimates.Rd

Combine point estimates and covariance matrices from a list of completed-data fits with Rubin's rules. Degrees of freedom use the Barnard-Rubin adjustment when df.com is finite. For a svysem_mi object, df.com defaults to the design degrees of freedom.

Usage

pooled_estimates(object, standardized = FALSE, level = 0.95, df.com = NULL)

Arguments

object

A list of objects with stats::coef() and stats::vcov(), or a svysem_mi object.

standardized

If TRUE, pool std.all standardized estimates. Correlations use the Fisher z scale.

level

Confidence level for ci.lower and ci.upper.

df.com

Complete-data degrees of freedom. For a svysem_mi object the default is the design degrees of freedom. NULL or Inf uses the large-sample Rubin degrees of freedom.

Value

A data frame with one row per parameter and columns est, se, t, df, p, ci.lower, ci.upper, riv, lambda, fmi and m.

Details

t is the t statistic, the pooled estimate divided by its standard error, not the total variance. With standardized = TRUE, each fit must be a lavaan object. Standard errors on that table are requested with se = TRUE, because lavaan omits them when the fit's class is not exactly lavaan. se = TRUE matches sqrt(diag(vcov())). Loadings, regressions and variances are pooled on the std.all scale. Correlations (~~ with different left- and right-hand sides) are pooled on the Fisher z scale, z = atanh(r) with se_z = se_r / (1 - r^2). Reported est, se and confidence limits are transformed back (est = tanh(z), se = se_z * (1 - est^2), limits tanh(z +/- t * se_z)). For those rows, t, df, p, riv, lambda and fmi stay on the z scale.

References

Rubin D (1987). Multiple Imputation for Nonresponse in Surveys. Wiley, New York. doi:10.1002/9780470316696

Barnard J, Rubin DB (1999). "Small-Sample Degrees of Freedom with Multiple Imputation." Biometrika, 86(4), 948–959. doi:10.1093/biomet/86.4.948

See also

pooled_wald(), svysem()

Examples

fit_once <- function(seed) {
  design <- simulate_design(n_psu = 6, n_per = 4, n_strata = 2, seed = seed)
  svysem(
    "y ~ x1 + x2", design,
    fixed.x = FALSE, meanstructure = TRUE
  )
}
fits <- list(fit_once(1), fit_once(2))
pooled_estimates(fits, df.com = fits[[1]]@df)
